Understanding Open Zoning in Larimer County

Open zoning (also known as zoning code “O”) is a unique land use designation in Larimer County, Colorado. It may sound flexible—and in some ways it is—but it also comes with limitations that can surprise first-time land buyers.

What Is Open Zoning?

Open zoning is generally intended to preserve views, reduce density, and limit large-scale development in rural areas. It’s most common in western Larimer County, near foothills or environmentally sensitive areas.

What Can You Do on Open Zoned Land?

  • Build a single-family home
  • Keep animals for personal use (check limits)
  • Apply for agricultural, conservation, or limited-use permits

You can typically build accessory structures like barns and shops—but commercial or multi-unit development is not allowed without additional approval.

Open zoning is not a blank slate—it has specific use restrictions and strict density requirements.

Density & Subdivision Rules

  • Minimum lot size is often 10–35 acres
  • Subdivision may be restricted or require a complex process
  • Water rights, septic, and road access must meet rural standards

Permits and Use Reviews

While you can live and build on most open-zoned parcels, any use beyond a primary residence (like a business or event space) may require:

  • Special Review Permit
  • Public hearings
  • Conditional use evaluation

How to Learn More

Always check the property’s zoning with the county before making an offer. Visit the Larimer County Planning website or contact zoning staff directly:

  • Larimer County Zoning Districts
  • Larimer County Planning Department
